name: drop_in_place
documentation:
Executes the destructor (if any) of the pointed-to value.

 See [`ptr::drop_in_place`] for safety concerns and examples.

 [`ptr::drop_in_place`]: crate::ptr::drop_in_place()
rules: For safety, `self` must be valid for both reads and writes.
For safety, `self` must be properly aligned, even if `T` has size 0.
For safety, `self` must be nonnull, even if `T` has size 0.
The value pointed to by `self` must be valid for dropping, including any type-specific invariants required for dropping it; for example, a `Box`'s heap pointer must be valid.
While `self.drop_in_place()` is executing, parts of the pointed-to value may be accessed only through the `&mut self` references supplied to the `Drop::drop` methods it invokes.
If `T` is not `Copy`, using the pointed-to value after calling `self.drop_in_place()` can cause undefined behavior. Assignment such as `*self = foo` counts as a use because it drops the value again.
After dropping the pointed-to value, `write()` may be used to overwrite its storage without dropping the old value again.
`self.drop_in_place()` may be used to drop pinned data when `T` is not `repr(packed)`; pinned data must not be moved before it is dropped.
